# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fidler_2018_olopatadine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fidler_2018_olopatadine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-018-9588-7> (open access, PMC6061088)

Olopatadine is an antihistamine and mast-cell stabiliser given as eye drops for
allergic conjunctivitis. Fidler et al. pooled two conjunctival allergen
challenge (CAC) trials and modelled the patient-rated ocular itching score
(0-4 in 0.5-unit steps, nine categories) as an ordinal outcome. No ocular
concentrations were measured, so the dose strength (%) enters a virtual
kinetic-pharmacodynamic (K-PD) compartment whose first-order washout drives an
Emax drug effect. The paper's purpose was to show which patients obtain better
24-h itching relief from olopatadine 0.7% than from 0.2%.

# Population

The model was fitted to 10,759 itching observations from 547 adults in trials
C-10-126 (NCT01479374) and C-12-053 (NCT01743027). The data were 3269 baseline
(screening) observations and post-treatment observations on vehicle (117
patients), olopatadine 0.1% (99), 0.2% (167) and 0.7% (164). Table 3 of the
paper (545 patients in the intention-to-treat analysis set) reports a mean age
of 40.9 years (range 18-77) and 60.2% women. The eye's baseline itching score
had a mean of 2.8 (SD 0.5), median 2.8 and range 1.5-4.0. Grass (42%), dust
mites (17%) and ragweed (17%) were the most common challenge allergens.
Patients had to show itching of at least 2 and redness of at least 2 in two of
three vessel beds at both screening challenges.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Fidler_2018_olopatadine")()$population`.

# Model structure

For itching score `s = 0.5, 1, ..., 4` the paper models

`logit P(Y >= s) = alpha_0.5 + ... + alpha_s + Ve(s) - De(s) + psi_BL (BL - 2.8) + eta`

with

* `Ve(s) = Vi * (Vb * (BL / 2.8)^psi_Vb + Vm * t) * prod_{m <= s} expit(v_m)`: the vehicle
  effect, on every record after a drop of vehicle or olopatadine (`Vi = 1`),
  with `t` the time since the drop;
* `De(s) = Emax * A / (EC50 + A) * prod_{m <= s} expit(delta_m)`: the drug
  effect, with `A` the K-PD amount (dose strength, %) washing out with a
  half-life of 18.46 h;
* an extra `psi_0.7 (BL - 2.8)` in the 0.7% arm after treatment.

The library stores the model in the `logit P(grade <= k)` frame of its other
proportional-odds models, with grade `k = 2 x score`. Every sign is therefore
flipped: `logite0 = -alpha_0.5` and `logitstep<k> = -alpha_s` with
`k = 2 s - 1`. The rxode2 ordinal endpoint `ocular_itch ~ c(p0, ..., p7)`
returns category `k` for itching score `(k - 1) / 2` in the `sim` column. The
model also outputs `itch_mean`, the expected score
`0.5 * sum_s P(Y >= s)`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Cumulative-logit model `logit P(Y >= s) = f_s + eta` | -- | Methods, 'Model development' equations |
| `f_s = De(s) + Ve(s) + sum alpha` | -- | Methods equation for `f_s` |
| `De(s)`, `Ve(s)` with differential-odds products | -- | Methods equations for `De(S)` and `Ve(S)` |
| Linear covariate shift `psi (cov - median)` | -- | Methods, 'Covariate analysis' equation |
| `logite0` | -8.79 | Table 5, alpha 0.5 = 8.79 (sign-flipped) |
| `logitstep1` .. `logitstep7` | 1.47, 1.03, 0.85, 1.88, 2.88, 3.02, 2.14 | Table 5, alpha 1 .. alpha 4 (sign-flipped) |
| `logit_placebo` | -4.98 | Table 5, 'Vehicle linear shift (Vb)' |
| `slope_placebo` | 0.06 1/h | Table 5, 'Vehicle time shift (Vm)' |
| `e_ocular_itch_bl_logit_placebo` | 2.16 | Table 5, 'psi baseline on Vb'; Table 4 'Baseline on vehicle (Vb)' |
| `logitfdiff_placebo1` .. `7` | 10 (fixed), 10 (fixed), 10 (fixed), 2.38, 1.07, 10 (fixed), 10 (fixed) | Table 5, column 'v s' |
| `lkel` | log(log(2) / 18.46) | Table 5, 'KPD drug half-life' 18.46 h |
| `lec50` | log(0.03) | Table 5, 'EC50 (%)' |
| `lemax` | log(3.40) | Table 5, 'Maximum effect, Emax' |
| `logitfdiff_drug1` .. `7` | 10 (fixed), 10 (fixed), 3.64, 1.56, 10 (fixed), -10 (fixed), 10 (fixed) | Table 5, column 'delta s' |
| `e_ocular_itch_bl_ocular_itch` | 5.37 | Table 5, 'psi baseline, distribution' |
| `e_dose_high_ocular_itch_bl_ocular_itch` | -0.64 | Table 5, 'psi Olopatadine 0.7 % shift on baseline, distribution'; Table 4 |
| `etalogite0` | 1.9044 (SD 1.38) | Table 5, 'Log odds SD (w)' |
| Centring value 2.8 | 2.8 | Table 3, overall median baseline itching |

# Typical-value check against the printed equations

A typical eye (`eta = 0`) is solved with the packaged model and compared with a
direct implementation of the paper's equations in its own `P(Y >= s)` frame,
using the Table 5 values. Both sides use the same parameters, so the difference
is pure numerical error and a tight bound is the right check.

```{r typical-check}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Fidler_2018_olopatadine"))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Paper-frame implementation (Methods equations, Table 5 values)
alpha <- c(8.79, -1.47, -1.03, -0.85, -1.88, -2.88, -3.02, -2.14)
v_s <- c(NA, 10, 10, 10, 2.38, 1.07, 10, 10)
delta_s <- c(NA, 10, 10, 3.64, 1.56, 10, -10, 10)
fac_v <- c(1, cumprod(plogis(v_s[-1])))
fac_d <- c(1, cumprod(plogis(delta_s[-1])))
paper_mean <- function(bl, trt, tad, amt, high) {
  ve <- trt * (-4.98 * (bl / 2.8)^2.16 + 0.06 * tad)
  de <- 3.40 * amt / (0.03 + amt)
  shift <- (5.37 - 0.64 * high * trt) * (bl - 2.8)
  f <- cumsum(alpha) + ve * fac_v - de * fac_d + shift
  0.5 * sum(plogis(f))
}

kel <- log(2) / 18.46
grid <- expand.grid(
  bl = c(2, 2.8, 3.5), dose = c(0, 0.2, 0.7), tchal = c(0.5, 16, 24),
  KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE
)
grid$id <- seq_len(nrow(grid))
ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  grid |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1, amt = dose),
  grid |> mutate(time = tchal + 5 / 60, evid = 0, amt = 0)
) |>
  mutate(
    cmt = "depot_kpd", TRT_PHASE = 1, OCULAR_ITCH_BL = bl,
    DOSE_HIGH = as.integer(dose == 0.7)
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
s_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame")
s_typ <- s_typ |>
  left_join(grid, by = "id") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(paper = paper_mean(bl, 1, time, dose * exp(-kel * time), dose == 0.7)) |>
  ungroup()
max_abs_diff <- max(abs(s_typ$itch_mean - s_typ$paper))
max_abs_diff
stopifnot(max_abs_diff < 1e-6)

# K-PD washout: the amount at 24 h is the dose times exp(-kel * 24)
kpd24 <- s_typ |> filter(dose == 0.7, abs(time - (24 + 5 / 60)) < 1e-9)
stopifnot(all(abs(kpd24$depot_kpd / (0.7 * exp(-kel * kpd24$time)) - 1) < 1e-4))
```

The typical expected score at the 24-h challenge for an eye with the median
baseline (2.8):

```{r typical-table}
s_typ |>
  filter(bl == 2.8) |>
  mutate(arm = ifelse(dose == 0, "Vehicle", paste0(dose, "%"))) |>
  select(arm, tchal, itch_mean) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = tchal, values_from = itch_mean) |>
  rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Onset (0.5 h)" = `0.5`, "16 h" = `16`, "24 h" = `24`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Virtual CAC cohort

Each simulated subject is one eye. The eye's baseline itching score is drawn
from a normal distribution with the Table 3 mean and SD (2.8, 0.5), redrawn
until it lies in the analysis-set range 1.5-4.0. The schedule follows the
C-10-126 design described in the Methods: a screening challenge (baseline
records), then a drop of study medication followed by a challenge 24 h later,
a drop with a challenge 16 h later two weeks on, and a drop with a challenge
27 min later (onset of action) one week after that. Itching is scored at 3, 5
and 7 min after each challenge. All four arms are solved with the same seed
and the same baseline draws, so they differ only in treatment.

```{r cohort}
n_per_arm <- 200
set.seed(20180421)
draw_bl <- function(n) {
  out <- rnorm(n, 2.8, 0.5)
  bad <- out < 1.5 | out > 4
  while (any(bad)) {
    out[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), 2.8, 0.5)
    bad <- out < 1.5 | out > 4
  }
  out
}
bl_draw <- draw_bl(n_per_arm)

h <- 24
visits <- tibble::tibble(
  visit = c("24 h", "16 h", "Onset"),
  dose_time = c(7 * h, 21 * h, 28 * h),
  chal_time = c(7 * h + 24, 21 * h + 16, 28 * h + 27 / 60)
)
make_events <- function(dose) {
  obs_min <- c(3, 5, 7) / 60
  ids <- seq_len(n_per_arm)
  base <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_min) |>
    mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, TRT_PHASE = 0, visit = "Baseline")
  doses <- expand.grid(id = ids, v = seq_len(nrow(visits))) |>
    mutate(
      time = visits$dose_time[v], evid = 1, amt = dose, TRT_PHASE = 1,
      visit = visits$visit[v]
    ) |>
    select(-v)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, v = seq_len(nrow(visits)), m = obs_min) |>
    mutate(
      time = visits$chal_time[v] + m, evid = 0, amt = 0, TRT_PHASE = 1,
      visit = visits$visit[v]
    ) |>
    select(-v, -m)
  bind_rows(base, doses, obs) |>
    mutate(
      cmt = "depot_kpd",
      OCULAR_ITCH_BL = bl_draw[id],
      DOSE_HIGH = as.integer(dose == 0.7)
    ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

arms <- c("Vehicle" = 0, "0.1%" = 0.1, "0.2%" = 0.2, "0.7%" = 0.7)
sim <- bind_rows(lapply(names(arms), function(a) {
  ev <- make_events(arms[[a]])
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180421)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, keep = "visit", returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(arm = a, score = (sim - 1) / 2)
}))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2: mean itching score by arm and challenge time

Figure 2 of the paper annotates each panel with the mean (SD) itching score of
its population-predicted simulation (100,000 subjects with between-subject
variability). The simulated mean below is the cohort average of the expected
score `itch_mean` over eyes and the three post-challenge times. The baseline
column pools the screening records of every arm. Olopatadine 0.1% was not
studied at the 16-h challenge.

```{r fig2-means}
fig2_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~visit, ~published,
  "Baseline", "Baseline", 2.86,
  "Vehicle", "Onset", 1.72, "Vehicle", "16 h", 2.11, "Vehicle", "24 h", 2.21,
  "0.1%", "Onset", 1.80, "0.1%", "24 h", 1.64,
  "0.2%", "Onset", 0.64, "0.2%", "16 h", 1.05, "0.2%", "24 h", 1.36,
  "0.7%", "Onset", 0.53, "0.7%", "16 h", 0.92, "0.7%", "24 h", 1.14
)
sim_means <- sim |>
  mutate(arm = ifelse(visit == "Baseline", "Baseline", arm)) |>
  group_by(arm, visit) |>
  summarise(simulated = mean(itch_mean), .groups = "drop")
fig2_cmp <- fig2_pub |>
  left_join(sim_means, by = c("arm", "visit")) |>
  mutate(difference = simulated - published)
fig2_cmp |>
  rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Challenge" = visit, "Figure 2 population mean" = published,
    "Simulated mean" = simulated, "Difference" = difference
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# The 0.1% onset annotation (1.80) disagrees with its own panel: the observed
# and individual-predicted means are 0.77 and 0.80, and the population bars
# put most of their mass at scores 0-1. It is checked against the observed
# mean instead and left out of the population-mean envelope.
typo_row <- fig2_cmp$arm == "0.1%" & fig2_cmp$visit == "Onset"
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a sign or scale error in any effect moves every arm's mean by
  # much more than this.
  median(abs(fig2_cmp$difference[!typo_row])) < 0.12,
  # Envelope on each arm-by-time mean of 200 eyes (not on a per-eye extreme).
  all(abs(fig2_cmp$difference[!typo_row]) < 0.3),
  abs(fig2_cmp$simulated[typo_row] - 0.77) < 0.3
)
```

The 0.1% onset panel of Figure 2 prints a population-predicted mean of 1.80,
but the same panel's observed and individual-predicted means are 0.77 and
0.80, and its population-predicted bars sit mostly at scores 0-1, which cannot
average 1.80. The annotation is read as a typesetting error for 0.80; the
simulated mean matches the observed 0.77.

```{r fig2-hist, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  mutate(arm = ifelse(visit == "Baseline", "Baseline", arm)) |>
  count(arm, visit, score) |>
  group_by(arm, visit) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    arm = factor(arm, levels = c("Baseline", names(arms))),
    visit = factor(visit, levels = c("Baseline", "Onset", "16 h", "24 h"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(score, pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_grid(visit ~ arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Itching score", y = "Percent of observations",
    caption = "Replicates the population-predicted bars of Figure 2 of Fidler 2018."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Figures 3 and 4: 24-h relief with olopatadine 0.7% versus 0.2%

The paper defines 24-h relief as an average itching score below 1 (or below
1.5) over the three post-challenge times. Figure 4 shows that olopatadine 0.7%
relieves itching in roughly 10-25 percentage points more patients than 0.2%,
with a difference that grows with the required screening severity. The paper's
own simulation selected patients by their screening scores; here the cohort is
stratified by the eye's baseline score instead, and the two arms share every
baseline draw and random effect.

```{r fig34}
relief <- sim |>
  filter(visit == "24 h", arm %in% c("0.2%", "0.7%")) |>
  group_by(arm, id, OCULAR_ITCH_BL) |>
  summarise(avg = mean(score), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    severity = cut(OCULAR_ITCH_BL, c(1.5, 2.5, 3, 4),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      labels = c("baseline < 2.5", "2.5 to 3", "baseline > 3")
    )
  )
relief_tab <- bind_rows(
  relief |> mutate(severity = "All eyes"),
  relief |> mutate(severity = as.character(severity))
) |>
  group_by(severity, arm) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    below_1 = 100 * mean(avg < 1),
    below_1.5 = 100 * mean(avg < 1.5),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
relief_tab |>
  rename(
    "Baseline stratum" = severity, "Arm" = arm, "Eyes" = n,
    "% relieved (mean < 1)" = below_1, "% relieved (mean < 1.5)" = below_1.5
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

relief_diff <- relief_tab |>
  select(severity, arm, below_1, below_1.5) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(below_1, below_1.5)) |>
  transmute(
    severity,
    diff_below_1 = `below_1_0.7%` - `below_1_0.2%`,
    diff_below_1.5 = `below_1.5_0.7%` - `below_1.5_0.2%`
  )
relief_diff |>
  rename(
    "Baseline stratum" = severity,
    "0.7% minus 0.2%, mean < 1 (points)" = diff_below_1,
    "0.7% minus 0.2%, mean < 1.5 (points)" = diff_below_1.5
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

all_eyes <- relief_diff[relief_diff$severity == "All eyes", ]
# Direction of the paper's conclusion: 0.7% relieves more eyes than 0.2%.
stopifnot(all_eyes$diff_below_1 > 0, all_eyes$diff_below_1.5 > 0)
```

As in Figures 3 and 4, olopatadine 0.7% relieves itching at 24 h in more eyes
than 0.2%, by about 10-20 percentage points overall (the paper's simulated
differences are 13-22 points). The gain is largest in the eyes with the most
severe baseline itching, where the paper reports about 25 points. Because
each stratum holds only 50-90 eyes, the per-stratum differences are
illustrative.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Sign of the drug effect.** The printed equation adds the drug effect
  `De(S)` to `logit P(Y >= s)` with a positive Emax of 3.40, which would make
  olopatadine raise itching. The model subtracts it, so olopatadine lowers the
  cumulative probability of every score. That is what Figure 2 and the trial
  results show.
* **Differential-odds factors.** The paper writes the factors as a product of
  `delta_m` (or `v_m`) but calls the parameters 'logit-transformed differential
  odds adjustment parameters', where 10 'implied no additional change to the
  odds' and -10 'implied the odds for this and larger scores approach zero'.
  The model uses the cumulative product of their inverse logits, which is the
  only reading consistent with that description (a literal product of the
  printed values would multiply the effect by up to 10^7).
* **Covariate centring.** The covariate equation subtracts the 'Median
  Covariate' without printing it. The model centres the baseline score at 2.8,
  the overall median in Table 3; the vehicle power term uses the same value.
* **Baseline score per eye.** The covariate is 'the average of all of the
  baseline measurements for the eye'. Each simulated subject here is one eye;
  the paper's random effect is per patient and is shared by both eyes, which
  this single-eye cohort does not represent.
* **Vehicle time.** `t` in the vehicle term is taken as the time since the last
  drop (`tad()` of the K-PD compartment). Vehicle-arm drops are `amt = 0`
  doses so that this time is defined.
* **0.7% shift.** The extra baseline-score shift of the 0.7% arm is applied
  only to post-treatment records (`TRT_PHASE = 1`), because baseline records
  precede randomisation.
* **EC50 units.** The paper states that the EC50 units 'are unknown, though
  could match the dose (which was measured in %)'. The model doses the strength
  in % into the K-PD compartment, so the EC50 of 0.03 is in %.
* **Figure 2 annotation.** The 0.1% onset population-predicted mean printed
  in Figure 2 (1.80) is read as a typesetting error for 0.80 (see the Figure 2
  section); that row is compared with the observed mean.
* **Population count.** The Methods text gives 547 patients; Table 3 lists
  545 in the intention-to-treat analysis set. The `population` metadata uses
  the 547 of the text.
* **Figure 4 replication.** The paper's 24-h relief simulation enrolled
  patients by screening criteria (2/6 to 5/6 baseline observations at or
  above a threshold) and sampled parameter uncertainty over 100 simulated
  studies. The table above uses fixed Table 5 values and stratifies by the
  baseline score instead, so it checks the direction and size of the 0.7%
  versus 0.2% benefit rather than reproducing each point.
* Age and sex were tested on Emax, the vehicle shift and the score
  distribution and were not retained (Table 4); they are documented in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
